text.p: Drinks and retailing group Allied Domecq Plc said it will pioneer the use of "virtual" television advertising in Britain on Saturday, making use of technology first developed for cruise missile guidance systems and Tomahawk jets.

The company will use the technology to place electronically "virtual" perimeter board advertising for four of its spirits brands on Sky Sports live coverage of the England Vs Australia rugby game to be played in Sydney, Australia.

The system will enable the company to insert pitch side boards onto the pictures without actually having the boards at the stadium. The brands British viewers will see in rotation are Laphroaig and Teacher's whisky, sherry Harveys Bristol Cream and Cockburn's port.

"It will revolutionise event and sports sponsorship and it will bring significant benefits to those who organise events because they can sell broadcast rights in a more meaningful way," said Mark Hunt, group communications manager at Allied Domecq.
"This is a great opportunity to test it in the UK market. This is a first and those brands are absolutely relevant to the UK market," he added.

The advertising will cost Allied 50,000 pounds ($84,300), including graphics, broadcast rights and technology. The company needed approval from the broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc Plc, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd is the largest shareholder, and the holders of the rights to the event, the Australian Rugby Football Union.

"For advertisers it will allow us to target our brands more effectively. For instance we may just want to advertise a particular brand in Germany which is not available in France and that in turn will give broadcasters the opportunity to generate revenue from a range of markets."

In theory it could provide the solution for sponsors of international sporting events who face a tobacco or alcohol advertising ban in certain countries, such as Canada or Britain's new legislation on tobacco advertising.
It would enable producers of sporting events in Britain for instance to insert digital billboards in transmissions to countries where tobacco advertising is legal.
Allied said it will fully evaluate the system and look at using it on its other brands like Ballantine's whisky which sponsors snowboarding and Teacher's sponsors of jazz events.
TV audiences in Britain for Sky's coverage of the game are estimated to exceed one million.
The system has been bought to Britain by International Sports Group. The system is owned by French based Lagardere Groupe.
